key_insight: BubbleSH provides a compact 3D dataset of rising deformable bubbles that captures both trajectory dynamics and shape evolution via spherical harmonics, enabling data-driven modeling of complex bubbly flows.
engineering_relevance: The dataset supports development and benchmarking of surrogate models for multiphase flow simulators where bubble interactions and deformation strongly affect system behavior.
method: High-fidelity direct numerical simulations of bubble swarms in a periodic domain.
Time-resolved recording of bubble trajectories, velocities, and deformable interfaces.
Compact shape encoding using spherical harmonics plus trajectory and shape prediction metrics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports transient 3D bubble-swarm data with proposed evaluation metrics for both trajectory and shape prediction, and benchmarks a probabilistic equivariant emulator on the dataset.
watch_item: Because bubble-swarm dynamics are highly sensitive to local perturbations, model evaluation and generalization may be unstable without careful handling of stochasticity and symmetry constraints.
paper_title: BubbleSH: A Dataset of Rising Bubbles with Deformable Interfaces
